text: तद्यथा ॐ भैषज्ये भैषज्ये भैषज्यसमुद्गते स्वाहा
meaning: "Thus: AUM, healing, healing, arisen from healing, so be it." A call to Bhaisajyaguru, the Medicine Buddha, whose vow is to ease the suffering of body and mind.
purpose: A prayer of care for one’s own healing, or another’s, alongside medical care.
when: Beside any treatment, never instead of it.
note: Recited across East Asian and Tibetan Buddhism. A spiritual practice, never a substitute for a doctor.
source: Bhaiṣajyaguru Sūtra (dhāraṇī as printed in the Wikipedia article on Bhaiṣajyaguru)
name: Medicine Buddha Mantra
iast: tadyathā AUM bhaiṣajye bhaiṣajye bhaiṣajya-samudgate svāhā
pronunciation: tad-ya-thaa AUM bhai-shaj-yay bhai-shaj-yay bhai-shaj-ya sa-mud-ga-tay svaa-haa; in Tibetan practice te-ya-ta AUM (said short) be-kan-dze be-kan-dze ma-ha be-kan-dze ra-dza sa-mud-ga-tay so-ha
